text:
maya: heads-up — thinking through a 'soft-eviction' autofallback for A/B rollouts. idea: layered fallback chain so we avoid full rollback unless necessary.

maya: proposed sequence: 1) model-variant degrade (smaller/quantized model), 2) regional failover for affected zone, 3) capacity-soft-degrade (serve from KV/prefix cache + shorter max_tokens), 4) instant reweight to control if quality or latency thresholds are breached.

jorge: +1. runtime should own the low-latency decisions (staging between 1–3) so we don't add RPC roundtrips. control-plane defines policy and SLO thresholds.

elena: important: quota & billing semantics. if traffic is reweighted to control, how do we attribute usage? we need explicit billing rules in rollout config.

samir: quality detection: add lightweight eval probes against a small prompt-set during canary, and compare top-k overlap / hallucination heuristics. if probes fail, escalate to reweight.

maya: agreed. also we need a decision provenance field in traces: who decided (runtime vs control-plane) and reason code.

maya: quick config sketch (pseudo-JSON) for console/runtime to agree on:

```
{  "ab_test_id": "ab-2026-03-20-17",
  "traffic_split": {"control":90, "variant":10},
  "fallback_policy": [
    {"stage":1, "action":"variant-quantized", "triggers":["p95_latency>250ms","error_rate>0.01"]},
    {"stage":2, "action":"region-failover", "triggers":["zone_capacity>0.9"]},
    {"stage":3, "action":"kv-degrade+shorten-max-tokens", "triggers":["cost_per_token>threshold"]},
    {"stage":4, "action":"reweight-to-control", "triggers":["quality_probe_failure"]}
  ],
  "decision_mode": "runtime-first", // or "control-only"
  "telemetry_tags": ["ab_test_id","fallback_stage","trigger_metric","decision_source"]
}
```

deploy-bot: Canary started for ab-2026-03-20-17 — 10% -> variant-b (quantized available)

sre-bot: alert: us-west latency p95 jumped to 320ms for variant-b — autoswap stage 2 triggered (region-failover) :rotating_light:

maya: good. runtime should perform region-failover automatically but emit a console event and an entry in the rollout timeline. we need an explicit 'rollback_hard' flag if operators want immediate full rollback.

jorge: implementation notes: runtime needs access to capacity/topology signals and must be able to target specific region endpoints. add a fast-path in serving runtime: `evaluateFallback(policy, metrics)` that returns next_action.

elena: UI: show timeline entry like "stage 2: region-failover — trigger=zone_capacity, source=runtime, previous_state=variant-b". also surface cost delta and expected latency change.

samir: runbook (short):
1) observe rollout timeline -> check quality probe metrics
2) if probe failure, confirm with quick sampling of responses (team-lead)
3) if confirmed, either force stage-4 reweight via console or patch policy to escalate faster
4) post-mortem: attach failing prompts and probe traces to the AB test

maya: also add metric tags in traces: `fallback_stage`, `trigger_metric`, `decision_source`, `ab_test_id` so alerting and dashboards can aggregate by stage.

jorge: we should also add a quota-safety check: if region-failover would exceed control capacity quota, runtime should skip to stage-3 instead of stage-2 and emit a 'quota-shortage' reason.

elena: +1. that keeps behavior deterministic and avoids cascading overload.

samir: we should gate automatic stage-4 (reweight) behind a confidence window (e.g., 30s sustained probe failure) to avoid flip-flopping.

maya: thanks. next steps: eng-runtime — can you prototype `evaluateFallback` + telemetry tags? eng-console — can you add a timeline event for auto-fallbacks and a way to force a stage via the UI/API? i'll draft a short RFC with the sketch above.

jorge: will prototype runtime patch this week.

elena: I'll mock the UI timeline entry and billing attribution flow.

samir: I'll write a simple probe harness and alarm rules.

maya: perfect — tagging @eng-runtime and @eng-console for visibility. :thumbsup:
